M4.5/3 · Feature UX · explorations for the gates
Companion · design workbench · 2026-08-09

Eight gates, on the real art

Every critter on this page is the shipped generated asset pushed through the real canvas-LUT duotone, with gear composited from anchors.json fits. Flip the hue and theme above — the whole page re-renders through the production pipeline. Each numbered section is one decision; options are lettered, and my recommendation is stamped. Pip belongs to whichever hue you pick; the flock keeps its own owners' hues on purpose.

01 · Widget anatomy

How the scene and the facts share the feature tile

The 2×1 feature slot on the kid dashboard (standard size, 20px inset, feature chrome). The scene is body + worn gear + props — the payoff surface for every milestone pick — and the facts are name, level, mood, and the meter to the next milestone, filled in the kid's own hue.

AScene left, facts rightRecommended

Props get the horizontal room they were drawn for (the 170-unit prop canvas), text never crowds the art, and the right column reads top-to-bottom as a sentence: who · how they feel · what's next.

States and the compact fallback

Anatomy A across its three tempers, plus the 1×1 compact variant (16px inset): critter, name, meter sliver — the mood line is the first thing to go. Milestone-ready is the only state that asks for a tap: the meter completes, the mood line becomes the invitation, and the punch-card's breathing dashed ring — the app's established "something waits here" mark — wraps the scene.

Perky · resting · milestone-ready at compact. Resting is dozing, never sad — nothing is lost on a quiet week. The ring + CTA replace mood only while a pick waits.

02 · The reaction moment

What "the critter noticed" looks like

When the chores XP flight lands (onFlightDone), the widget acknowledges it. No care loop — this is the whole feedback vocabulary. Replay each candidate on the live widget:

PipLv 3
Feeling perky today
40 XP to Lv 4

A (recommended): one squash-and-stretch hop — same 420ms weight class as the punch stamp — with a sparkle burst at the apex while the meter banks the XP. The hop acknowledges; the meter is the receipt. B reads as ambient decoration, not notice. C restates what the flight and meter already said — two receipts for one event. Reduced motion: meter + sparkle fade only, no displacement.

03 · The hatch

Where the flow interrupts, and what "later" leaves behind

A (recommended): auto-open once, egg waits. First dashboard visit after launch opens the flow once — full-screen sheet on mobile, dialog on desktop. "Later" dismisses forever; the widget then holds the egg, and tapping it reopens the flow. Tier 4 enters the same flow from Settings. B (egg only, never interrupts) leaves launch day unannounced — a kid who never taps never hatches. C (block the dashboard until hatched) gates chores and the wallet behind a cosmetic choice. 04 · The wardrobe

Equip: slot rows or a shelf grid

Tapping the widget opens the existing Drawer — full-screen sheet on mobile, 440px right rail at md:+, same as chore capture. Both variants below are live: tap to dress Pip. A (recommended): slot rows — five slots, tap a row to expand that slot's owned items plus None. Slots make swaps legible ("the cap replaced the horns because they share a head") and give bare slots a visible home. B: shelf grid — every owned item in one grid, tap to toggle. Fewer taps while the collection is six items, but the slot rules become invisible side effects, and None has nowhere to live.

05 · The flock

Everyone's critters on the family dashboard

Species shape + owner hue are the two identity channels (ADR 044) — the flock never needs a label to say whose critter is whose, but it carries name + owner anyway because show-off value is half the point. A (recommended): the shelf — a single lineup, worn gear only (props stretch a strip unevenly; they live on the kid's own widget and the wardrobe). B: member rows — an ItemCard list that useFitRows clamps naturally, at the price of the flock reading as another chore list. Unhatched: an egg waits only for profiles that will hatch (tiers 1–3 before first visit, or a parent who opted in). A parent who never opts in simply isn't in the flock — no permanent egg nag.

06 · The level curve

Pacing the track against a real week

At the ~175 XP/week baseline (ADR 056 economy), each ruler places every milestone on the calendar. A (recommended): the draft becomes final — 50 · 150 · 300 · 500 · 750 · 1,050 · 1,400 · 1,800. First prize inside two days, then a milestone every 1–2 weeks, stage-ups landing at week 2 and week 8 — exactly the hatchling/kid/teen age reads the assets were built to. Lv 8 is max level for v1; content drops extend the track. B: extend to Lv 10 (2,250 · 2,750) — sixteen weeks of runway, but the last picks arrive a month and a half apart and the offer pool runs thin. Hover any marker.

Unchosen items may return at later milestones (ADR 061), so no offer ever needs the four parked items — they stay the backlog for the renderer extensions.

Mood windows

Mood is derived at read time from XP recency — nothing stored, nothing punitive. One threshold: perky within the window since the last XP, resting beyond it. Dots are chore completions across a sample two weeks (a busy weekday run, a skipped weekend, one quiet stretch). 48h is the recommendation — one off day never dims the critter, but a genuinely quiet stretch reads as a nap, which is what invites the tap back.

24h
48h ★
72h

Filled = perky, gray = resting. 24h flickers on any normal week; 72h barely ever rests. Milestone-ready overrides mood while a pick waits.

07 · The milestone moment

Who hears about a level-up, and where

The kid's copy respects the currency registers: XP in a sentence is spelled out, quiet star, no gold. Routed as priority: 'alert' — toast + tray for the kid (tiers 1–2 never get push; the ring on the widget is the durable signal, so nothing is lost). For the parent, three candidates:

08 · The home-layout amendment

Where the companion and the flock live, per surface

The ADR 061 placement made concrete against home-layout.ts. Kids: companion takes the feature; the wallet steps down beside it; feed drops below the fold (elevation and reading order still agree in every column). Teens: same order, no feature — the teen surface declines to shout (ADR 039 amendment), so the companion leads by position only. Parents + the family tablet: no companion widget of their own — the flock joins as a full-width quiet strip; an opted-in parent's critter appears there, and a personal widget waits for the layout editor.

Considered and set aside: a split default_layout_family key restoring the feed banner for the wall tablet — a second divergence to maintain for one surface, and the flock-at-bottom serves the fridge fine; and a 2×1 flock slot — half the family is clipped at four members.
